confounders: X (the 12 anonymized customer features) is the primary *observed* confounder candidate: if it affects both who gets treated (in an observational assignment mechanism) and the outcome, it opens a back-door path T <- X -> Y that must be closed by adjustment (regression adjustment / IPW / DR). U (unobserved intent, budget, engagement) is a potential *unobserved* confounder -- if it affects both assignment and outcome, no amount of adjustment on X alone identifies the effect; this is the key threat to validity in the observational scenario discussed in Section 6.3.
mediators: E (exposure -- whether the ad was actually delivered/seen) and V (site visit) both sit on the causal path FROM the campaign TO conversion: T -> E -> V -> Y. They explain *how* the campaign works, but must never be conditioned on when estimating the causal effect of T on Y -- adjusting for a mediator blocks part of the very effect being measured and biases the estimate toward zero (this is why the ATE analysis in this project always compares outcomes by the ORIGINAL treatment assignment T, i.e. an intent-to-treat analysis, never by realized exposure or visit).
colliders: V (Visit) is simultaneously a mediator (T -> V) and a collider on the path T -> V <- U -> Y, because unobserved browsing propensity U also drives visits. A common real-world mistake is to compute 'conversion rate among visitors' by arm -- this conditions on the collider V, opening a spurious U-induced association between T and Y that does not reflect the campaign's true causal effect. This project deliberately avoids conditioning on V or E anywhere in the ATE/CATE estimation.
identifiability: Scenario 1 (randomized, the ACTUAL Criteo assignment mechanism): the dashed U->T and X->T edges are absent by design, so the back-door path through X and U is closed automatically and ATE = E[Y|T=1] - E[Y|T=0] is identified without any adjustment. Scenario 2 (hypothetical observational assignment, e.g. a marketer manually targets high-value segments): if only X drives targeting, the effect remains identifiable via back-door adjustment on X (regression adjustment / IPW / DR, conditional on positivity and no unmeasured confounding). If U also drives targeting AND affects Y outside of X, the effect is not identifiable from observational data alone -- adjustment on X is necessary but not sufficient, and the residual bias direction/magnitude is unknown without an instrument or a natural experiment.
